title: Raise the floor

predict.q: The government guarantees $25 and buys the surplus. The floor rises to $30. What happens to the government's bill?

options.s: It falls, because farmers now earn enough without help
options.fb: Farmers' incomes do rise, but the state is still buying every unsold unit, and now there are more of them, each at a higher price.

options.s: It rises, because it buys a bigger surplus at a higher price
options.fb: The surplus doubles from 30 to 60 thousand and each unit costs $30: the bill rises from $750k to $1,800k.

options.s: It stays the same, because the surplus does not change
options.fb: A higher floor makes buyers buy less and producers make more, so the surplus grows.

task: Move the floor slider and watch Qd, Qs and the shaded government-spending rectangle. Then try the demand-elasticity settings.

target.do: Raise the floor from $25 to $30, then press Check.

takeaway: A higher floor and more elastic demand and supply mean a bigger surplus and a bigger bill.
